_schema: LEGEND governance v3.1.1 · Annex A.1 TASK_ASSIGNMENT (operator-directed) + A.1b
OBJECTIVE: Without interrupting live sessions, establish whether the runtime exposes an up-to-date measure of the 5h and 7d quota windows and their reset time; separate what the interface shows, what software can read, what the model can reach, and what can actually be stopped and resumed; design the stop-and-resume path; and prove checkpoint, halt and resume on a harmless task before building any general resumer.
runtime_audited: Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.269; three live sessions running throughout, none interrupted
constraints_honoured: no quota figure derived from context size
no JavaScript injected, no internal socket called
layer_1_interface: the panel receives rate_limit_event carrying rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows, relays it as panel_usage_update, and draws a bar per window with a percentage and a reset time - five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet and a model_scoped list. LIVE, and unreachable by a local process. Bars are HIDDEN below 70 percent (u_1 = 0.7): a quiet panel is not evidence of a quiet quota.

layer_2_software.cache: ~/.claude.json cachedUsageUtilization: fetchedAtMs, per-window utilization and resets_at, plus a limits[] array with severity, is_active and a per-model scope. NO REFRESH GUARANTEE.
layer_2_software.refusal_record: a transcript record's quotaLimits appears ONLY when a request is refused: 15 records here, ALL status rejected, ALL rateLimitType five_hour, never the weekly window. Carries resetsAt but NO consumption level.

layer_3_model: NOTHING. No tool returns quota; a tool search over usage, quota, rate, limit, consumption and reset returns only unrelated tools. claude --help lists 17 subcommands and none is a usage or quota command; claude agents --json carries pid, cwd, kind, name, sessionId, startedAt, status and no usage field.
layer_4_stop_resume: children: YES, demonstrated. This session: NO. claude agents --json reports every session here as kind interactive; stop, attach and respawn address BACKGROUND sessions. The 2026-09-11 audit established the native wait-for-reset requires an interactive TTY the panel does not provide.

the_measurement_that_decides_it.five_hour: 13 percent, resets_at 22.5 hours IN THE PAST
the_measurement_that_decides_it.seven_day: 84 percent, resets_at 17.1 hours IN THE PAST
the_measurement_that_decides_it.weekly_scoped: 90 percent, severity critical, is_active true, scope Fable
the_measurement_that_decides_it.consequence_1: freshness must be read from fetchedAtMs and NEVER from the file mtime: the config is rewritten for unrelated reasons while the block is not
the_measurement_that_decides_it.consequence_2: nine samples one a minute across 7.6 minutes of continuous LLM traffic gave ONE distinct fetchedAtMs: nothing observed refreshes it, so a local waiting loop CANNOT detect a reset
the_measurement_that_decides_it.the_operators_own_point_confirmed: the 5-hour window stood at 13 percent while a scoped weekly limit stood at 90 percent, critical and binding. A 5-hour reset would not have helped.

built.quota_state.py: read and record. Reports the AGE FIRST, lists every window separately, keeps severity, is_active and per-model scope. Exit 0 fresh, 1 stale or reset-already-passed, 2 no reading at all. record appends one timestamped JSON line per call.
built.absence_is_a_result_never_a_zero: four absence paths each exit 2 and say which: key missing, file missing, malformed JSON, and a block carrying no fetchedAtMs - the last because a percentage whose age cannot be established is not a reading
built.test_quota_state.py: 14 tests, expectations written by hand against hand-written fixtures; no test reads the live cache, since a suite asserting against it would pass on a fresh day and fail on a stale one

demonstration.task: deliberately harmless: digest and line-count three repository files, one checkpoint per step plus one append to a progress log, writing only to a scratchpad
timeline: halted mid-task with TaskStop while step 2 had not begun
after the halt: step1.json complete, step2.json and step3.json ABSENT, log exactly 1 line, digests recorded
21:13:2x resumed by message to the same agent
demonstration.verified_after: step1.json digest UNCHANGED (ae6c0ebe…), log exactly 3 lines with no duplicate, each checkpoint present once
demonstration.the_agents_own_words: it skipped step 1 because its checkpoint was already complete
demonstration.detail_worth_keeping: the resumed run saw a REFUSED tool call from before the halt in its replayed history and said it could not tell whether that command had run. The checkpoint on disk, not the transcript, told it the truth - an argument for checkpoints carrying a digest.

path_designed_and_what_is_proved.1_trigger: reader PROVED; the TRIGGER IS NOT RELIABLE because the reading can be a day old
path_designed_and_what_is_proved.2_stop_new_assignments: proved trivially - no new delegation after the halt
path_designed_and_what_is_proved.4_ordered_halt: PROVED for a child; for this session the halt is the end of a turn
path_designed_and_what_is_proved.5_external_wait_with_no_llm_calls: PROVED - the recorder is pure local I/O
path_designed_and_what_is_proved.6_verify_the_reset_actually_happened: NOT PROVED AND NOT LOCALLY VERIFIABLE. The cache does not refresh, so the only software-visible evidence of a reset is a successful request after the reset time, or a fresh refusal carrying a new resetsAt. The clock is not evidence; a wall-clock timer would resume into a still-closed window.

missing_capabilities: no supported way for a LOCAL PROCESS to obtain a FRESH quota reading. The live figure exists - the panel draws it - but it arrives over the extension's private host-to-webview transport, is not written to any log, and the on-disk cache carries no refresh guarantee. Consequence: the trigger and the reset verification both rest on a possibly stale reading, so the design must treat 'quota unknown' as the normal case.

no supported way to resume THIS session after it stops: every session here is kind interactive, the background-session commands do not address it, and the native wait-for-reset needs a TTY the panel does not provide
single_operator_action_that_remains_nece: after the reset, send one message in this panel to this session. Nothing else needs a human: children are stopped and resumed programmatically, checkpoints are honoured, and incomplete-only resumption was demonstrated without duplication.
limits: one extension version on one machine, one account
the cache's refresh behaviour was observed for 7.6 minutes, not over a reset boundary; it may refresh on an event not seen here, and an unobserved refresh is not proof that none exists
no refusal occurred during the audit, so the quotaLimits path was read from 15 historical records and not exercised live
the panel's live event was traced statically in the installed bundle, not intercepted
the demonstration used one child and three steps: it shows the primitives work, not how they behave under a real quota refusal
named windows such as nimbus_quill and tangelo appear with null or zero values and are reported as found, not interpreted
DEFAULTS_TAKEN: A reader with a staleness verdict was built because the mandate asked for a way to record the datum with a timestamp and detect absent or stale data. No resumer, no daemon, no timer.
The harmless demonstration used one in-process child, stopped with TaskStop and resumed by message, since that is the only stop/resume pair the runtime exposes to this session.
A background sampler was used to measure cache refresh and was stopped when its measurement was sufficient.
